answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a forge as the anchor of the cost.
